summary: Muhammad Ashraf Khan is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He has served as Director at Quaid-i-Azam University (attested 2019) and the Department of Archaeology and Museums, Andhra Pradesh, and as Deputy Director at Taxila Museum.

Specializing in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, Muhammad Nasim Khan earned an M.Phil from the University of Peshawar. His career includes posts at Peshawar (attested 2006–2016), the University of Hamburg (attested 2006), and the Royal Asiatic Society.

Muhammad Shahidullah (1885–1969) worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Calcutta and under Sylvain Lévi in Paris. His career included long-term positions at the University of Dhaka (~1921–1954), Rajshahi University (~1955–1958), and the Bangla Academy (~1960–1967).

Muhammed Niyas Ashraf works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the Free University of Berlin (2015–2024) and held a postdoctoral fellowship at Ghent University (2025–2026).

Mukesh Mehta specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his Ph.D. at Banaras Hindu University (2019–2022) and served as a Research Associate at the International School for Jain Studies in 2023.

Mukund Lalji Wadekar is an Indologist. He served as Officiating Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 2002–2008) and Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 2008), as well as General Editor for Gaekwad's Oriental Series (attested 2008).
Mukund Ram Shastri (d. 1921) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Head Pandit at the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir (attested 1911 and 1916–1918).

Mukunda Raj Aryal specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned an MBA from Apex College (2011–2013) and an M.Phil. from Tribhuvan University (2019–2021), where he was attested as professor in 2003, later heading Apex College (2017).

Mumon Yamada (1900–1988) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hanazono University and under Seisetsu Seki. He served as president of Hanazono University (1949–1978), abbot at Shofuku-ji (~1949–1978), and head of the Institute for Zen Studies (1964).

Mun-keat Choong works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Queensland under Roderick S. Bucknell, later serving as Lecturer in Studies in Religion at the University of New England (2003–2025).

Munenobu Sakurai (b. 1961) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. After completing doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1984–1989), he served as an assistant professor at Iwate University and professor at Tohoku University (~2005).

Muneo Tokunaga (1945–2016) was an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University and earned a PhD from Harvard (~1971–1974). He held faculty posts at Kyoto University (1979–1980, ~1989–2009) and Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1980–1989).

Muneyoshi Yanagi (1889–1961) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1910 to 1913 and was a student of Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki (~1909–1913).

Mungunchimeg Batmunkh specializes in religious studies, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Batmunkh completed a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna under the doctoral supervision of Brigitte Marschall (attested 2010).

Munis D. Faruqui (b. 1967) is an Indologist and historian. He served as Associate Professor at the University of California, Berkeley in 2005 and as Director and Professor at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (~2014).

Munish Chandra Joshi (1935–2007) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (~1989–1993) and Member Secretary at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (~1998–2004).
Munkhjavkhlan Baatar is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who completed a PhD and held an academic post at the National University of Mongolia.

Murray Barnson Emeneau (1904–2005) worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Oxford and Yale under Franklin Edgerton. He taught at Yale (1926–1939) before serving at the University of California, Berkeley (1940–1971) as Assistant Professor of Sanskrit and General Linguistics.

Murray Fowler (1905–1999) worked in linguistics and Indology, receiving his Ph.D. from Harvard under Joshua Whatmough. He held teaching posts at Pomona College, Purdue, Harvard, and as Associate Professor of comparative philology at Wisconsin-Madison (1946–1953).

Musashi Tachikawa (b. 1942) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Nagoya and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, later holding professorships at Nagoya, the National Museum of Ethnology, and Aichi Gakuin University.
